newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian says not asking AMR to buy more.
newsitem.headline: Canadian says not asking AMR to buy more.

text.p: Canadian Airlines is not asking 33-percent owner AMR Corp to up its stake in the ailing carrier, even though the Canadian government said on Wednesday it was open to examining any such proposal, a Canadian Airlines spokeswoman said.
"It's not even being considered at this point," said Canadian's Claudia Cattaneo.

However, Canadian would favor being allowed to attract more U.S. investors, something currently prohibited by regulations that say non-Canadian investors cannot hold more than 25 percent of its voting shares, Cattaneo said.
Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR has 25 percent of Canadian's voting stock and a total 33 percent economic interest.
Canadian as part of its survival plan is asking AMR for a cut in fees it pays for computer and reservation services. AMR said last week it was not considering upping its stake.
Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said in Ottawa on Wednesday that the federal government would examine any proposal by AMR to increase its holding.
"There's been no request for an equity investment from them," Cattaneo said.
AMR officials were not immediately available for comment.
The governments of Canada, Alberta and British Columbia also said on Wednesday that they allowed the carrier to defer the principal on government-backed loans for one month.
Canadian has about C$30 million outstanding after repaying most of the C$120 million in loans.

But Canadian officials reiterated that, despite a call for a government bailout from the airline's major unions, the company was not preparted to ask for more public money to help dig out of a possible cash crunch. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
